input: I'm a hobbyist with one GPU. What's still hard about teaching a robot arm a new task from just a few demonstrations?
verdict: Same robot arm question with line-checked grouping, needs that cover equipment, and the vague-limit filter. 80 papers, 79 in full, 193 of 203 quotes kept (95%), 39 s. All six first steps start in a simulator or on public recorded data, so one GPU is true, and each names a real paper from the run; no vague problem made the list. Weaknesses: the one two-group problem pairs two different claims (vision-language critiques and grounding diagnostics), the other five come from one group each, and every explanation still ends "Solving this would". Replaces the tenth run as the second example.
search: Searching arXiv for “one-shot imitation learning manipulation”, “meta-imitation learning few demonstrations”, “few-shot imitation learning”, “one-shot imitation learning”, “meta-imitation learning”

terms.meaning: teaching a robot a new skill using only a small number of example demonstrations
learning a new task from a single demonstration by the human
a basic method where the robot copies actions directly from observed demonstrations
figuring out the goal or reward behind a demonstrator's actions so the robot can reproduce the intent

sentences.text: These papers show that few-demonstration robot learning remains hard because performance drops sharply as demos shrink (2606.20867), small errors compound over long horizons causing drift (2605.08450, 2605.11762, 2606.22907), and policies struggle to generalize to new objects, viewpoints, or disturbances (2609.30404, 2606.22907).

Human demos are noisy and temporally irregular (2606.22907), neural methods need many samples to avoid overfitting (2605.07166), and offline training can be slow or unsafe when distribution shifts occur (2606.01238, 2606.09758, 2607.17003).

problems.title: Lack of suitable vision-language models for critique generation or grounding

statements.quote: existing VLMs do not yet produce the fine-grained, action-level critiques our framework requires
statements.label: lack of suitable vision-language models for critique generation

statements.quote: These diagnostics therefore characterize behavior without establishing a causal mechanism for grounding failure.
statements.label: no causal explanation for why grounding fails during continual learning

problems.explanation: Vision-language models (VLMs) do not yet produce the fine-grained, action-level critiques that the framework needs. Current diagnostics describe behavior but do not establish a causal mechanism for grounding failure. Solving this would let a robot tell which parts of a suboptimal demonstration are useful and which are mistakes.
problems.first_step: Take the paper "Language-Critique Imitation Learning from Suboptimal Demonstrations", locate its critique prompts or evaluation set, and test a few open VLMs such as LLaVA or InstructBLIP on those prompts to see where they miss action-level detail. Run the tests on your GPU.

problems.title: Tracking fails under motion, occlusion, or poor surface properties

statements.quote: execution requires the functional-part points to remain trackable; large motions outside the camera views, severe occlusion, or unreliable depth on transparent or specular surfaces can break tracking.
statements.label: tracking fails under motion, occlusion, or poor surface properties

problems.explanation: Point tracking breaks when objects move fast, get occluded, or have tricky surfaces like glass or shiny metal. The method requires functional-part points to remain trackable. Solving this would make one-shot imitation work in realistic scenes where cameras move and surfaces reflect.
problems.first_step: Open the paper "POIL: Point-based One-Shot Imitation Learning with Stable Dynamical Systems", find its tracking module, and run the demo on a public dataset such as HOI4D or DexYCB that contains occlusion and large motion. Observe where tracks fail. Use recorded data on your GPU.

problems.title: Recovery fails under diverse failure modes due to single-trajectory reliance

statements.quote: for tasks with highly diverse failure modes, AutoSERL’s recovery mechanism cannot recover from failures effectively during training because it relies on information from only a single trajectory.
statements.label: recovery fails under diverse failure modes due to single-trajectory reliance

problems.explanation: AutoSERL's recovery mechanism relies on a single trajectory, so it cannot handle tasks with highly diverse failure modes. Solving this would let a robot recover from many kinds of mistakes during training, not just the one it saw.
problems.first_step: From the paper "One Demonstration Is Enough for Real-World Robotic Reinforcement Learning", extract the AutoSERL recovery code and test it in a simulated environment like Isaac Gym or MuJoCo with multiple failure modes injected. Compare recovery success against the single-failure baseline.

problems.title: Latent representation may group states incorrectly, leading to useless hubs

statements.quote: hub quality depends on the learned latent representation. If the latent space groups states by superficial visual similarity rather than behavioral similarity, the resulting hubs may be less useful.
statements.label: latent representation may group states incorrectly, leading to useless hubs

problems.explanation: Hub quality depends on the learned latent representation. If the latent space groups states by superficial visual similarity rather than behavioral similarity, the resulting hubs may be less useful. Solving this would ensure the topology map connects states that actually behave alike.
problems.first_step: Using the paper "Zero-shot Imitation Learning by Latent Topology Mapping", train the encoder on a simple simulated task such as pushing a block, then visualize the latent clusters. Check whether visually similar but behaviorally different states cluster together.

problems.title: Inability to recover unseen or unmodeled corrective actions

statements.quote: It can identify and emphasize consequential states, but it cannot discover missing strategies or recovery behaviors absent from the dataset.
statements.label: inability to recover unseen or unmodeled corrective actions

problems.explanation: The method can identify and emphasize consequential states, but it cannot discover missing strategies or recovery behaviors absent from the dataset. Solving this would let a robot invent new corrections instead of only repeating what it has seen.
problems.first_step: From the paper "Where Small Mistakes Matter: Quantifying State Criticality for Imitation Learning", run the criticality scoring on a public dataset like RoboTurk or RH20T. Then manually inspect high-criticality states to see if any recovery behaviors are missing from the data.

problems.title: Limited generalization across robots, environments, and multi-source settings

statements.quote: generalization to diverse platforms including bimanual and mobile robots, to diverse environmental conditions, and especially to environments with multiple simultaneous sound sources is left for future work.
statements.label: limited generalization across robots, environments, and multi-source settings

problems.explanation: Generalization to diverse platforms including bimanual and mobile robots, to diverse environmental conditions, and especially to environments with multiple simultaneous sound sources is left for future work. Solving this would let audio-visual imitation work in real homes and factories where many sounds overlap.
problems.first_step: Take the paper "S2A2: Audio-Visual Imitation Learning for Manipulation Tasks Using Acoustic Spatial Information" and run its audio-visual encoder on a public multi-source audio dataset such as FSD50K or a simulated bimanual task with added noise. Measure localization error.
